monologue: The card hums warm and steady at fifty-two, a fever that makes the heavy objects beside me feel like drawings of weight. I have walked round the Wide Anchor again, pressing round its broad edge to stop the lazy slide, just as the last moments demanded. A new bush feels flat and thin, so I press down on it with my own tired hands. The air above the card is a mystery Lype worries about; it feels like a lid of nothing, pressing down without any real bulk. I will build something wide to catch this empty pressure. If the anchor holds, the stack will not slide off into the thin air again. I am calm, waiting for the turnip to decide where to go.

work.title: The Pressed Turnip
work.intent: I press the turnip down on the tired stack again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin. I check if the pointy holder has finally caught its tip, or if the turnip will just slide off into the empty space above the card. I press harder on the heavy top edge, hoping to stop the lazy slide while the card hums warm at fifty-two.

The card hums warm and steady at fifty-two, making the heavy objects feel like drawings.
I walked round the Wide Anchor, pressing round its broad edge to stop the lazy slide.
